record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Adding population dynamics to dynamic-memory models
record.original_question: For any of the dynamic-memory movement models introduced in Section 2.2.2, how do the dynamics change when demographic birth and death processes are added to the movement equations rather than assuming pure movement? In particular, do time-dependent or steady-state solutions still exist, and how do spatially non-constant steady-state profiles change after demographics are included?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13. How do the dynamics of any model introduced in Section 2.2.2 change when birth/death processes are also included? Do solutions exist solving the time-dependent or steady state problems? How do solution profiles change for spatially non-constant steady state solutions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a class of partial differential equation models describing the movement of an animal population with density u(x,t) on a bounded spatial domain Ω ⊂ ℝ^n (n = 1, 2) with no-flux boundary conditions, coupled to a dynamic cognitive memory map k(x,t) representing the animal's spatially distributed knowledge of resource quality or familiarity. A representative form of such a "dynamic-memory" model is

  ∂_t u = ∇·[ D ∇u − u χ ∇(G ∗ k) ],          x ∈ Ω, t > 0,
  ∂_t k = α u − β k + δ Δk,                   x ∈ Ω, t > 0,

together with no-flux (Neumann) boundary conditions on u and k and non-negative initial data u(·,0) = u_0 ≥ 0, k(·,0) = k_0 ≥ 0. Here D, χ, α, β, δ ≥ 0 are constants, and G ∗ k denotes a spatial convolution of k with a nonnegative perception kernel G (so the advective velocity is determined nonlocally by the memory field k). Variants in this class include replacing the gradient ∇(G ∗ k) by ∇k itself, allowing the memory equation to be a pure ODE (δ = 0), and allowing different forms of the perception operator.

Pure-movement models of this type conserve total population: ∫_Ω u(x,t) dx = ∫_Ω u_0(x) dx for all t ≥ 0.

Augment any such model by adding demographic birth and death terms to the equation for u, producing

  ∂_t u = ∇·[ D ∇u − u χ ∇(G ∗ k) ] + f(u),     x ∈ Ω, t > 0,
  ∂_t k = α u − β k + δ Δk,                    x ∈ Ω, t > 0,

with no-flux boundary conditions, where f : [0,∞) → ℝ is a smooth reaction term modeling net population growth (for example logistic f(u) = r u (1 − u/K) with r, K > 0).

Address the following:

(a) Establish global existence, uniqueness, and non-negativity of classical (or appropriate weak) solutions (u, k) of the demographically augmented system for suitable initial data u_0, k_0.

(b) Determine the set of steady-state solutions (U(x), K(x)) of the augmented system, i.e. solutions of
  ∇·[ D ∇U − U χ ∇(G ∗ K) ] + f(U) = 0,
  α U − β K + δ ΔK = 0,
with no-flux boundary conditions. In particular, identify conditions on D, χ, α, β, δ, the kernel G, the domain Ω, and the reaction f under which non-constant (spatially heterogeneous) steady states exist.

(c) Compare these results with the corresponding pure-movement case f ≡ 0: describe quantitatively how the existence, multiplicity, stability, and spatial profiles of non-constant steady states are altered by the inclusion of f, and whether demographics can create, destroy, or qualitatively reshape the pattern-forming behavior of the pure-movement model.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicitly open question in a list of open problems on PDE models for animal movement with nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping. No published resolution covering existence theory and steady-state structure for these dynamic-memory models with added demographics was located; related work treats pure-movement variants or simpler memory-free nonlocal models, leaving the demographically augmented dynamic-memory case open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems concerning nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping PDE models, including effects of birth/death processes on dynamic-memory movement models.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed among open problems with no resolution provided.
